title: Oscars visual effects race advances to 20 films, with Dune and The Odyssey among contenders
body_md:
The visual effects competition for the 99th Academy Awards has entered another preliminary stage. According to the exclusive report available in the historical feed, the Academy's Visual Effects Branch informed the teams behind 20 films that their work had advanced. The report identifies 19 of those productions, leaving one title unconfirmed.

This distinction matters because the Academy does not publicly release this internal top-20 list. The reported selections are not the official ten-film shortlist and should not be described as Oscar nominations.

Disney leads the confirmed group with four productions: Avengers: Doomsday, Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu, Whalefall and the live-action Moana. These films represent different approaches to visual effects, ranging from large-scale fantasy environments to creatures and digitally augmented physical photography.

Denis Villeneuve's Dune: Part Three is another prominent contender. Both previous Dune installments won the visual effects Oscar, giving the filmmaker an opportunity to extend that record. However, the third movie must still advance through additional stages before it can compete for the award itself.

Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey and Steven Spielberg's Disclosure Day also appear in the reported field. Both filmmakers have histories of working on productions recognized for visual effects. Phil Lord and Christopher Miller's Project Hail Mary joins them, alongside Digger, Supergirl and The Sheep Detectives.

The preliminary group also illustrates the category's potential breadth beyond conventional Hollywood blockbuster production. Takashi Yamazaki's Godzilla Minus Zero, Laika's stop-motion feature Wildwood and the Indian epic Ramayana: Rise of a Legend represent distinctive national, technical and artistic approaches.

Additional reported selections include Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Jumanji: Open World, Backrooms, Heart of the Beast and The Mosquito Bowl. Backrooms is particularly notable as a feature from a young filmmaker whose earlier work found an audience online.

The report indicates that some major studio productions did not advance. Nevertheless, the absence of a title from this stage does not necessarily reflect its overall artistic quality or its prospects in unrelated awards categories.

Preliminary shortlist voting runs from December 7 through December 11, 2026, with the official shortlists scheduled for December 15. Visual effects presentations will follow in January, and the nominations are scheduled to be announced on January 21, 2027.

The 99th Academy Awards ceremony is scheduled for March 14, 2027. Until the official shortlist and nominations are released, any prediction about the ultimate winner remains speculative.

Will Villeneuve complete a visual effects trilogy sweep, or could Nolan's The Odyssey emerge as the stronger contender?
